title: First Post
text: Welcome to my first post here on my website! I plan to share any miscellaneous thoughts here, things that I just want to get out into the world.

title: Mario Truong
section: I can juggle 5 at a time.
text:
I can juggle 5 at a time.
When I was young, I got a book that teaches the reader how to juggle. I learned how to actually juggle (very poorly) from this, but quickly got bored, relegating the book to the depths of my closet.
Then, all of a sudden, my sister starts picking up juggling through her high school chemistry teacher. As a brother, my instincts kicked in–I needed to beat her at juggling.
The rest is history. I have attended international juggling festivals, the 47th annual MadFest, and am the treasurer (kinda) of my local juggling club. Juggling is fun, and I encourage anyone interested to learn how to juggle!

title: About Me
text:
Where I’m From
I am a UCLA student from Wisconsin. Growing up, mathematics was always interesting to me, but it took me until high school to realize that I had an affinity for the precise language of proofs, and that I could apply my mathematical knowledge towards creative problem solving in physics and computer science. From there, I followed my passions all the way back to California, decades after my parents moved out of California.







The view on the way to UCLA

title: About Me
text:
Academics
Currently, I am a second year undergraduate at the University of California, Los Angeles. I am an applied mathematics major, and my interests include differential equations, simulations, and optimization. I am a member of the College Scholars Program, and am pursuing the Departmental Honors Program as well as a computing specialization.

title: About Me
text:
Experiences






Design, Build, Fly at UCLA
I am currently a member of the aerodynamics subteam, where I conduct computational fluid dynamics simulations, post processing data analysis, and trade studies. Learning how to use software such as SimScale and XFLR, as well as being part of a team of engineers taught me the effective communication and collaborations skills required of engineers.























TraffiX
I worked with two other team members to code a traffic simulation package. Presenting this project to others required describing a technical model in intuitive terms, meaning this project challenged both my communication and coding skills. We worked with NetworkX and integrated OSMNX to glean real-world data to simulate for this project. Overall, learning how to build a model from scratch taught me how to apply careful observation about the world around us to a mathematical problem.









NASA and the Wisconsin Space Grant Consortium’s Aerospace Jam
I worked on a drone for a competition inspired by NASA’s Ingenuity mission. I coded an arduino to control a claw, ultrasonic sensor, and an air pump via an Android app. Competition day was nerve-wracking, but my teammates and I persevered and had an amazing experience designing, building, and testing our drone.

title: My name is Mario Truong.
text:
Currently, I am a student at the University of California, Los Angeles where I study applied mathematics.
Innovation occurs through the effective communication of creative ideas. I strive to be an advocate for ideas, whether that means fighting to support my own original work or amplifying the voices of others.


My Future
At the moment, I plan on pursuing graduate school in order to go into the field of operations research. I am drawn to this field as a result of my interest in mathematical simulation and modeling, as well as its wide range of applications. Additionally, this field significantly impacts many lives by speeding up ambulance response times, optimizing city planning, and planning organ transplant allocation.

title: Wait, you actually clicked on this?
text:
Growing up, I used to go on special trips with my mom to a Japanese supermarket in a suburb of Chicago. Inside this supermarket is a stationery store, which I would spend hours at a time in, exploring all of the different pens and pencils.
I started collecting pencils, first. I liked all of the different mechanisms. Auto-rotating lead, shake-to-advance, twisting erasers. From there, I moved on to pens.

title: Wait, you actually clicked on this?
text:
My collection
 Currently, I own a ballpoint Cross Bailey, an Ohto Liberty (in UCLA colors, of course), a Caran d’Ache ballpoint, and a Kaweco sport (with a great green ink) to name a few of my pens. As far as pencils, my two favorites are the Tombow MONO Graph and the UNI \(\alpha\)-gel switch.
As a math major, my obsession with handwriting doesn’t end there, either! I love a good chalkboard, and pretty much anything to do with handwriting, notation, or the art of putting ideas into the physical world.
